According to a news article seismicity during the month of October was characterized by 129 tornillo earthquakes, five low-frequency earthquakes, 28 shallow volcanic earthquakes, and 79 deep volcanic earthquakes; there were increases in the daily average of shallow volcanic earthquakes from less than two to nine per day and in the daily average of deep volcanic earthquakes from less than four to five per day. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) reported additional details about the moderately explosive eruption that occurred at Mayon during 1153-1159 on 30 October. The eruption produced a dense, billowing, gray ash plume rapidly rose 3 km above the summit and drifted SW. Dense parts of the lower ash plume collapsed and generated small-volume pyroclastic density currents (PDCs) that traveled 1.5-2 km down the Bonga (SE) and Basud (E) drainages. The eruption at Nevados de Chillán was ongoing during 5-11 November based on reports from the Servicio Nacional de Geología y Minería (SERNAGEOMIN), the Servicio Geológico Minero Argentino (SEGEMAR), and the Buenos Aires Volcanic Ash Advisory Center (VAAC). On 8 November the Buenos Aires VAAC reported that a period of continuous ash emissions were identified in satellite images rising to 4.6 km (15,000 ft) a.s.l. and drifting SW. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that at 1711 on 5 November a white-and-gray ash plume rose 500 m above the crater rim of Tengger Caldera?s Bromo cone and drifted W. The event lasted for 46 seconds based on seismic data. White steam-and-gas plumes rose as high as 600 m above the crater rim and drifted in various directions during 4-11 November. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4), and visitors were warned to stay outside of a 1-km radius of the crater.

The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported ongoing eruptive activity at Minamidake Crater (Aira Caldera?s Sakurajima volcano) during 2-9 November. An eruptive event at 1111 on 3 November generated an ash plume that rose 1 km above the crater rim and drifted SE. An explosion at 2217 on 5 November produced an ash plume that rose 1.4 km above the crater rim and drifted SE. Large blocks were ejected 800-1,100 m from the vent. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that no eruptions at Akan (also known as Meakan-dake, which means Meakan Peak) of the Akan volcanic complex were recorded after 15 March; unrest continued to decline. Sulfur dioxide emissions averaged 300-400 tons per day (t/d) during February-April but declined to 100-200 t/d starting in June. Steam-and-gas emissions also became less dense and vigorous. Seismicity began to decrease in June and was characterized as low in October. The Alert Level was lowered to 1 (the lowest level on a 5-level scale) at 1000 on 4 November.

The Alaska Volcano Observatory (AVO) reported that slow lava effusion continued to feed a thick flow in Great Sitkin?s summit crater during 4-9 November based on webcam and satellite images. The S flank of the dome slowly advanced and generated occasional small rockfalls. Minor earthquakes consistent with the growth of the lava dome were detected by the seismic network. Weather clouds obscured webcam and satellite views during most of the week, though warm surface temperatures over the active lava dome were identified in overnight satellite images during 7-8 November. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Ibu continued during 5-11 November, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Daily gray ash plumes rose 200-600 m above the summit and drifted in multiple directions. Incandescence at the summit was occasionally visible in webcam images. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second lowest level on a four-level scale) and the public was advised to stay 2 km away from the active crater and 3.5 km away from the N crater wall opening.

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Karangetang?s North Crater (Kawah Dua), characterized by the effusion of incandescent material, occasional small explosions, and periodic ash plumes, continued during 5-11 November. At 1314 on 5 November a dense white, gray, and brown ash plume rose 800 m above the summit and drifted S and SW. A dense white-and-gray ash plume rose 1 km above the summit and drifted SW at 1734 on 7 November. At 1914 on 9 November a dense white-and-gray ash plume rose 1 km above the summit and drifted NW. The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by incandescence, intermittent spatter, lava fountaining, and lava flows from vents along the SW and W margins of Halema`um`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 4-11 November. During an overflight early on 4 November scientists observed roiling lava ponds in both the N and SW vents. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported continuing eruptive activity at Lewotolok during 5-11 November. White-and-gray ash plumes rose as high as 100 m above the summit and drifted W and NW on 5 November, then as high as 300 m above the summit on 10 November with drifts NE, NW, and W. White plumes rose around 100 m above the summit on most other days. Webcam images showed incandescent material being ejected above the summit and onto the flanks on multiple days. The active lava flow on the SE flank was 600 m long. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4). Th

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity at Marapi (on Sumatra) continued during 5-11 November. Eruptive events were recorded during 5, 7-8, and 12 November by the seismic network, but were not visually observed due to weather conditions and/or darkness. The Alert Level remained at 2 (on a scale of 1-4) and the public was warned to stay 3 km away from the active crater.

The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that the eruption at Merapi (on Java) continued during 5-11 November, with avalanches produced by the active lava dome on the upper SW flank. As many as four daily lava avalanches traveled as far as 2 km down Krasak and Sat/Putih drainages on the SW flank; weather conditions sometimes obscured views. The Alert Level remained at 3 (on a scale of 1-4), and the public was warned to stay 3-7 km away from the summit, based on location.

The Servicio Geológico Colombiano (SGC) reported that eruptive activity at Puracé continued during 3-9 November. Seismicity indicating fluid movement beneath Puracé and Piocollo volcanoes at depths less than 3 km was at similar levels to the previous week. Seismic signals related to rock-fracturing were located 12-18 km NE at depths of 7-11 km, beneath the Puracé and Piocollo volcanoes at depths of 1-3 km and had low magnitudes, and 4-6 km SE of Puracé at depths of 5-6 km. The Instituto Geofísico-Escuela Politécnica Nacional (IG-EPN) reported that eruptive activity at Reventador continued at a high level during 4-11 November. Seismicity included 63-89 daily explosions, long-period earthquakes, harmonic tremor, and tremor associated with emissions. Daily ash-and-gas plumes were visible in webcam images and reported by the Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center rising as high as 1.5 km above the crater rim and drifting in multiple directions. The Observatorio Vulcanologico y Sismologico de Costa Rica-Universidad Nacional (OVSICORI-UNA) reported that minor eruptive events at Rincón de la Vieja continued to be periodically detected by the seismic and infrasound network during 4-11 November. These eruptive events were sometimes accompanied by steam-and-gas plumes. One of the plumes rose as high as 1 km above the crater rim during the morning of 5 November. The Alert Level remained at Level 2, Yellow, the second lowest level on a four-level scale.

The Instituto Geofísico del Perú?s (IGP) Centro Vulcanológico Nacional (CENVUL) reported continuing eruptive activity at Sabancaya during 2-8 November. The seismic network detected 17 seismic events associated with the movement of magmatic fluids, along with earthquakes indicating internal rock fracturing; no volcanic explosions occurred during the week. Gas, steam, and ash emissions periodically rose as high as 600 m above the summit and drifted less than 10 km SW and W. The Instituto Geofísico-Escuela Politécnica Nacional (IG-EPN) reported that volcanic activity at Sangay continued during 4-11 November. The seismic network recorded 3-19 daily explosions, a few long-period earthquakes, a period of harmonic tremor, and 6-13 daily signals indicating emissions. On most days the Washington Volcanic Ash Advisory Center reported that ash-and-gas plumes were visible in webcam views and satellite images rising as high as 1.5 km above the crater rim and drifting mainly NW, W, and SW. The Pusat Vulkanologi dan Mitigasi Bencana Geologi (PVMBG) reported that activity continued at Semeru during 5-11 November, with daily eruptive events recorded by the seismic network. Plumes of variable combinations of white, gray, and black rose 100-1,000 m above the summit and drifted mainly S, SW, and W on most days; emissions were not visible due to weather conditions on 9 November. According to news articles multiple pyroclastic flows were recorded by the seismic network and/or visually observed descending the Kobokan drainage on the SE flank during 4-6 November. The Kamchatkan Volcanic Eruption Response Team (KVERT) reported continuing lava effusion and explosive activity at the lava domes along the N crater floor of Young Sheveluch (on the SW flank of Old Sheveluch) during 4-11 November. A thermal anomaly was identified in satellite images on most or all days. Explosions on 5 November produced ash plumes that rose 5.7 km (18,700 ft) a.s.l. and drifted 80 km ESE. The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) reported that eruptive activity at Suwanosejima?s Otake Crater continued during 30 October-6 November. Intermittent eruptive events produced ash plumes that rose as high as 500 m above the crater rim. The Alert Level remained at 2 (the second level on a five-level scale) and the public was warned to be cautious within 1.5 km of the crater.
